title: Git in 60 seconds
caption: Git in 60 seconds: commits, branches and merges, and why nothing you commit is ever really lost.

scenes.say: Without version control, you end up with final, final two, and final real. And no idea what changed between them.
Git is built on three ideas.

items.title: Commit
items.say: A commit is a snapshot of your whole project, with a message saying why.

items.title: Branch
items.text: a movable pointer to a commit
items.say: A branch is just a name pointing at a commit, so making one is instant.

items.title: Merge
items.say: A merge joins two branches back together.

scenes.say: So you can try something risky on its own branch, and main never notices.
Every commit can be brought back. That's Git. Commit often, branch freely.
